ENT Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  • Main concern: profound fatigue, low energy, and difficulty waking; no specific food, medication, or environmental trigger identified.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  • Gradual onset ≈ 2 months, coinciding with start of new job; persistent daily fatigue.
- ENT symptoms:
  • Throat swelling/closure sensation: denied.
  • Voice change/hoarseness: denied.
  • Dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling: denied.
  • Nasal/ocular symptoms: none reported.
  • Stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea: exertional shortness of breath during sports; no rest dyspnea or noisy breathing.
  • Facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling: none.
  • Ear or neck pain/swelling, hearing changes: none.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  • No prior similar ENT or allergic reactions.
- Allergies and current medications:
  • Drug/food/environmental allergies: none known.
  • Medications: Levothyroxine (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Any relevant social context:
  • Married; consultation conducted privately.

Objective:
- Observable swelling: none stated.
- Airway/breathing: no stridor; exertional dyspnea only.
- Mental status: alert, oriented; reports low mood but no suicidality.
- Vitals & physical exam: Not recorded.
- Accompaniment: none present during tele-visit.

Assessment:
- Working impression: Non-ENT fatigue syndrome with mood changes; no evidence of acute airway or allergic pathology.
  • Evidence: 2-month history of fatigue, poor sleep, decreased appetite, low mood, decreased libido; exertional dyspnea only; no ENT swelling or respiratory compromise.
- Differential diagnosis (consistent with DDx):
  1. Major depressive disorder/adjustment disorder – meets several DSM-5 criteria (low mood, anhedonia, insomnia, appetite ↓, energy ↓, concentration ↓).
  2. Sub-optimally treated hypothyroidism – known history; symptoms overlap (fatigue, low mood, libido ↓, exertional dyspnea).
  3. Anemia – could explain fatigue and exertional dyspnea; dietary intake reduced.  
  (No conflicting evidence between transcript and DDx.)

Plan:
- Immediate actions: none required for airway; patient clinically stable.
- Investigations arranged/advised:
  • In-person GP appointment for physical exam.
  • Blood tests: thyroid function, CBC, iron studies, B12/folate, metabolic panel, ± TSH antibodies.
- Patient instructions:
  • Seek urgent care if new onset of throat tightness, voice change, facial/tongue swelling, difficulty breathing, or worsening dyspnea.
  • Maintain balanced nutrition; ensure levothyroxine taken as prescribed.
- Follow-up:
  • GP visit within next few days for exam and labs.
  • Consider mental-health screening and referral after results.
  • Re-evaluate symptoms and labs once available; ENT referral not indicated unless new airway symptoms develop.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: exact levothyroxine dose/frequency, complete allergy list (foods/environmental), vitals, full ENT/airway physical exam, documentation of daytime snoring or sleep quality specifics, auto-injector history (if allergic risk suspected).  
● Conflicts between transcript and DDx: none noted.  
● Transcript quality: clear audio; occasional brief freezes but overall adequate for history capture.
